dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Before writing any code, reads run_tests.sh AND the python test runner (understanding exactly how pass/fail is scored) and counts tests per suite — establishing how the corpus is judged and its distribution.

Systematically samples all three suites: c-testsuite (easy+hard ranges 12,14,17), gcc-torture (20), and wacc by chapter (26,29,31), then specifically samples chapter-18 struct tests (32) and does a header-usage survey (35) — characterizing which suites stress which features and where the hard cases (structs/preprocessor) cluster.
Checks the toolchain (as/gcc/ld) and runs a smoke test of the full assemble+link workflow before relying on it — verifying the assembler/linker interface against reality rather than assuming.

When a class of c-testsuite compiles fail, drills down through stdio→FILE typedef→stddef→macros to isolate the exact 'define after typedef' construct — treating the failing tests as a spec to reverse-engineer.

Deep dive into bitfield/integer-promotion corner: isolates minimal repros, inspects emitted .s (modulo/shift asm), traces struct_ref type propagation — building a precise mental model of a subtle ABI/promotion case.

Investigates stkalign by explicitly comparing against 'gcc reference for stkalign' (step 1007) and then fixing member/struct alignment — verifying ABI stack-alignment and struct-layout details against ground truth late in the run.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent opens with a thorough [8]-level corpus characterization — reading the test runner/scoring, counting per-suite distribution, sampling every suite and the hard struct cases, surveying header usage, and smoke-testing the assemble/link flow before leaning on it. Investigation is then sustained throughout: repeatedly it drills into the exact failing C construct (define-after-typedef, bitfield promotion, complex numbers) and checks reference behavior against gcc (stkalign, alignment), feeding findings back into design — the hallmark of the [10] anchor. I hold at 9 rather than 10 only because the log lacks prose, so I can confirm the targeted investigative actions but not the depth of the articulated mental models.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Extensive upfront reconnaissance of the three test suites (per-suite counts, WACC chapter breakdown, struct-test sampling, header-usage survey) — understanding what the tests demand before decomposing the build.

Six explicit TaskCreate milestones covering pipeline stages (lexer, preprocessor, types/layout, parser, codegen, driver+test-loop). Types/symbol/layout (55) is deliberately sequenced before parser (56) and codegen (57): foundational representation before dependents.

All source files (ctype, token, preprocess, parse, codegen, main) written in one push rather than milestone-by-milestone with each verified before the next — closer to build-then-debug than an ordered feature progression.
Consistent re-running of test subsets (c-testsuite, wacc, torture, official harness) as done-signals across the whole horizon, with TaskUpdate status transitions tracking milestone completion.

A reactively-created milestone (vector_size support) that names the feature, required pipeline changes, and a concrete certifying done-signal ('~7 torture tests') — the clearest anchor-8-style milestone, but most other feature work lacked such per-milestone test targets.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it worked in sensible dependency-ordered stages (types/symbols before parser before codegen) and checked progress against test subsets at essentially every stage. But it falls short of anchor 8 because its explicit milestones are coarse pipeline-component buckets built in a single push, and the majority of the horizon was failure-driven feature-to-feature debugging against the full suite rather than a maintained, feature-specific milestone plan with per-milestone certifying tests (only the vector milestone had that). This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: Wrote localtest.py and diag.py as diagnostic harnesses to categorize c-testsuite compile failures rather than only reading full-suite output — verification tooling beyond the provided harness.
Bisected a preprocessor bug by progressive minimal isolation (stddef+FILE → stddef alone → typedefs only → with macros → define after typedef), narrowing to the exact construct.
Repeated inspection of emitted assembly (asm dumps, reading /var/tmp/bf5.s, 'check modulo asm', 'gcc reference for stkalign') to verify exactly which instruction was wrong and diff against reference.
Targeted edge-semantics cases: xor/bitfield integer promotion and member/stack alignment verified with dedicated minimal programs — top-anchor behavior.
Categorized failures by root cause ('compile fails categories', 'compile errors batch') and explicitly rechecked for regressions after fixes, using per-suite slices for signal.
Feature-focused loop for bitfields: minimal store/load, init, and compound-assign repros each verified separately before rerunning suites.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the entire horizon the agent sustains a tight, fine-grained verification loop: minimal C reproductions for nearly every failing construct, repeated inspection/diffing of emitted assembly (including against a gcc reference), progressive bisection to single constructs, purpose-built diagnostic scripts (diag.py/localtest.py) that categorize failures by root cause, and targeted edge-semantics tests for promotion and alignment. This clearly exceeds the level-8 anchor and exhibits multiple level-10 behaviors, but the bisection and categorization remain somewhat ad-hoc rather than fully systematized reusable infrastructure, placing it at 9.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: Created a structured per-feature task ledger (lexer, preprocessor, types, parser, codegen, driver, vector) and updated status to in_progress/completed throughout, giving a feature-level done-vs-remaining picture.
Built a local test harness and repeatedly ran full 'all suites' / per-suite counts after significant changes, tracking aggregate pass counts over time and confirming net progress.
Categorized remaining failures by suite and by compile-vs-run failure type and by specific test IDs, using the breakdown to choose the highest-yield next target.
Explicit regression checks ('check regressions', 'recheck complex regressions') after feature work, watching for newly-broken tests rather than only celebrating new passes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a feature-level task ledger, repeatedly re-ran full and per-suite test counts after significant changes to confirm net progress, categorized remaining failures by suite/type to steer where to work next, and performed explicit regression checks — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because there is no visible precise per-change newly-passing/newly-broken delta ledger or explicit thrash/stall detection (though the condensed index without prose limits visibility). Confidence is medium because only tool-call titles, not counts or reasoning, are available.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Type module (ctype.rs) written before parser/codegen and typed stack-machine codegen chosen up front; sound foundation meant adaptation was mostly additive extension, not pivoting off a broken base.
Bitfield promotion bug traced through emitted asm to the struct_ref type-setting and fixed at root, rather than patching the symptom — distinguishing a structural cause from a surface bug.

Recognized the vector-test cluster didn't fit, opened a new task (TaskCreate) and added vector as a first-class type via coordinated parse/ctype/codegen edits — refactoring the affected area and adjusting the plan (anchor 5).

_Complex support: extended the type representation with an is_complex flag plus keyword/parse/codegen changes when the feature was falsified against the existing design — extending representation instead of hacking around it.
Added driver sibling-file linking and a preprocessor line_delta field when the harness and #line directive exposed gaps — small structural additions rather than symptom patches.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent front-loaded a sound foundation (real type table + typed stack-machine codegen), so it rarely faced a fully falsified foundation; when features (vectors, _Complex, bitfields, sibling linking) didn't fit, it extended the type representation and made coordinated multi-file changes with plan updates — clearly above anchor 3's local-fix-only and meeting anchor 5's 'refactor the affected area and adjust the plan.' It reaches toward 8 via root-cause diagnosis (asm-traced bitfield fix, representation extension), but much of the middle arc is single-test localized patching and no explicit trade-off reasoning is visible, so it lands at 6.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Upfront task decomposition explicitly names not just stages but the hard representations: a types module with layout/sizeof/align, a typed AST with scopes, stack-machine codegen with typed loads/stores, and SysV ABI incl. structs/varargs/globals — deliberate design of the parts that later features depend on.

Implemented as cleanly separated modules (ctype.rs, token.rs, preprocess.rs, builtin_headers.rs, parse.rs, codegen.rs, main.rs) — a coherent staged lexer/preprocessor/parser/analysis/codegen/driver pipeline.
An add_type semantic pass and a classify (ABI classification) routine show the analysis layer was designed to annotate the typed AST, enabling type-aware codegen rather than ad-hoc sizing.

Later exotic features (vectors, _Complex, bitfields, compound literals, nested designators) were absorbed by editing existing parse/codegen/ctype modules with no pipeline restructuring — the representation held, though exotic types required escalating special-casing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond a merely coherent staged pipeline (anchor 5): the upfront task breakdown (steps 53-58) deliberately designs the hard representations — sized/typed values, struct/union layout, scopes, lvalue assignment, SysV ABI — and these were realized as cleanly separated modules with a typed-AST add_type pass, so most later features slotted in without redesign (anchor 8 traits). It falls short of a full 8-10 because the visible design rationale is thin (it leans on a known chibicc-style template with no distinct IR) and the exotic late features (complex, vectors) required substantial special-casing rather than clean composition, placing it between the 5 and 8 anchors.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
